history.rationale: Sequence alignment of the human catalytic (TIM-barrel/FAD) domain with E. coli MetF maps the strictly conserved A-L-R-G-D motif (human A155-L156-R157-G158-D159) onto MetF A116-D120, whose Asp120 is the essential catalytic acid. Conservative D->N removes the carboxylate charge while keeping sterics, a classic catalytically null substitution.
Same conserved catalytic aspartate as above; alanine truncation deletes the side-chain carboxylate entirely and should abolish proton transfer/FAD chemistry while leaving the fold largely intact.

Arg157 (verified R at position 157 in the ALRGD motif) is a documented severe MTHFR-deficiency residue and sits adjacent to the catalytic Asp; loss of the guanidinium removes substrate/FAD electrostatic anchoring.

Gly158 in the invariant ALRGD active-site loop requires backbone flexibility and minimal side-chain volume; introducing a large, charged arginine should sterically and electrostatically wreck the catalytic loop.

Glu63 lies in the conserved EFFPPRT motif that aligns with E. coli MetF Glu28, an active-site residue implicated in proton donation to FAD N5; isosteric E->Q abolishes the acid/base function without gross structural change.
Same conserved active-site glutamate; alanine removes both charge and bulk, expected to give a near-null enzyme while preserving the N-terminal barrel fold.

Thr227 (verified T at 227 in the FIITQ region of the catalytic barrel) is a reported severe MTHFR deficiency site; the bulky hydrophobic methionine in this buried, conserved position should destabilize the FAD-binding core.
Arg335 (verified R) is a reported severe-deficiency residue in the linker/catalytic interface; loss of a conserved salt bridge plus an unpaired cysteine should strongly impair folding and activity.
Arg183 (verified R) is a conserved surface/interface arginine in the catalytic domain reported in MTHFR deficiency; charge loss likely reduces activity, though effect may be partial.

Verified A at 222; the classic thermolabile variant that promotes FAD release and reduced activity, but it is only a partial loss-of-function, so it is a lower-priority hedge for the 'abolish' objective.
